<!-- PR title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] muse-spark: Build the routed-MoE routing metadata on the router stream -->

## Motivation

In a decode MoE layer two streams run after the attention boundary:

- main stream: the pre-expert projection (pooler), the all-gather, then the pre-expert RMSNorm + NVFP4 quant;
- router stream: the router GEMM and the top-8 routing.

After the two streams join, the main stream calls FlashInfer's `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`, which first builds the routing metadata and then runs the expert GEMMs. The metadata depends only on the top-8 ids, so it does not need to wait for the main stream.

This PR builds the routing metadata on the router stream right after the top-8, and the main stream runs only the expert GEMMs after the join.

**GB300 is not affected by this PR.**

## Modifications

- `routed_moe_split.py` (new): `RoutedMoeSplit` holds the routing metadata for one token count, shared by all layers; `populate()` builds it on the router stream and `run_body()` launches FlashInfer's expert body from it. It uses FlashInfer 0.7.2's prepared-routing objects (`DABodyRunner`), with the runner and arguments adapted from `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe_op`. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8050 makes this a public argument (`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe(..., routing_metadata=...)`); `run_body` switches to it once SGLang requires a FlashInfer release that has it.
- `routed_moe_split.py`: `split_enabled` gates the split by `_SPLIT_MIN_TOKENS[(capability, tp)]`, the measured smallest token count where it wins (SM107 TP4 / TP8: 8); unlisted (GPU, TP) pairs keep the fused routing.
- `muse_spark.py`: `MuseSpark1xMoE` builds the split on the router stream after the top-8 when it applies (NVFP4, not Marlin, decode CUDA graph capture, enabled for this GPU and TP, M <= 1024 and FlashInfer's default tile <= 128) and passes it to the experts. `routed_moe_split` (and the FlashInfer internals it uses) is imported only once the cheap checks pass, so importing the model does not import it.
- `muse_spark_fp4_moe.py`: the experts call `moe_split.run_body` instead of `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` when a split is given; the arguments and outputs are the same.

The expert body's buffers are allocated per call like the ordinary routed call, so under CUDA graph capture they come from the graph pool shared by every captured batch size; only the routing metadata (a few small buffers per token count) is kept.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

The expert outputs are bitwise those of the ordinary routed call, so model outputs do not change.

Muse Spark Open + this PR, DFlash (real acceptance), sgl-eval with T=1.0, top_p=1.0, top_k=64, xhigh reasoning; GSM8K max 65K tokens, AIME26 30 problems x 16 repeats, max 131K tokens.

| GPU | TP | GSM8K | AIME26 pass@1 | AIME26 pass@16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SM107 | 4 | 97.65% | 96.67% | 100% |

<details>
<summary>Kernel tests</summary>

`test_muse_spark_routed_moe_split.py` (registered on `4-gpu-b200`, one GPU), bitwise against `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe(do_finalize=False)` (per-token weighted sum of the expert outputs): 64 local experts of 256 at M in {1, 16, 128, 512, 1024} and 32 local experts at M in {1, 16, 128, 512, 768} (TP4 / TP8 with EP), each with static and per-token activation scales. As in serving, the metadata is populated on a side stream and the main stream waits on it before the body; a CUDA graph of that sequence is then replayed twice with new routing and new activations copied into its inputs, each replay checked against an ordinary call on the same inputs. Gate tests assert the listed cases are admitted, tile 192 / M > 1024 are not, and only the measured (GPU, TP) pairs enable the split.

- SM107: 22 / 22 passed.

This PR requires the pinned FlashInfer 0.7.2: on 0.7.0.post1 the prepared body at tile 128 (32 local experts, M = 768) writes NaN into valid FC2 rows, while on 0.7.2 it is bitwise equal to the ordinary call.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

**Setup.** Base = our Muse decode stack with #47517 (fused all-gather + norm + NVFP4 quant), this PR = the same stack + this PR; FlashInfer autotune off and per-token NVFP4 activation off on both sides.

- SM107: base = main `c7994e7076` + #46724 + #47174 + #47517. 

### End to end (nsys)

**SM107 TP4** (one run per side)

| c | M | main | router | metadata | later stream, base | later stream, this PR | experts start (µs) | saved (µs) | layer (µs) | projected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8 | 7.0 | 9.1 | 3.0 | router | router | 13.5 -> 12.5 | +1.0 | 85.9 | -1.1% |
| 2 | 16 | 7.2 | 9.4 | 3.5 | router | router | 14.5 -> 12.7 | +1.8 | 98.6 | -1.8% |

**SM107 TP8** (median of four runs per side)

| c | M | main | router | metadata | later stream, base | later stream, this PR | experts start (µs) | saved (µs) | layer (µs) | projected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8 | 6.8 | 8.4 | 2.9 | router | router | 11.8 -> 11.2 | +0.6 | 70.4 | -0.8% |
| 2 | 16 | 6.9 | 8.6 | 3.8 | router | router | 12.9 -> 11.6 | +1.3 | 81.6 | -1.5% |
| 4 | 32 | 7.7 | 6.7 | 4.1 | main | router | 12.4 -> 9.6 | +2.8 | 89.5 | -3.0% |
| 8 | 64 | 9.5 | 9.5 | 4.2 | tie | router | 14.4 -> 12.6 | +1.8 | 106.8 | -1.6% |
| 16 | 128 | 10.2 | 10.4 | 3.8 | tie | router | 14.8 -> 13.8 | +1.0 | 119.5 | -0.8% |
| 32 | 256 | 13.1 | 12.1 | 4.3 | main | router | 17.9 -> 15.4 | +2.5 | 145.2 | -1.7% |
| 64 | 512 | 17.3 | 15.1 | 4.6 | main | router | 22.2 -> 18.8 | +3.4 | 208.5 | -1.6% |
| 128 | 1024 | - | - | - | main | main | not engaged (FlashInfer's default tile at 32 local experts is above the gate) | - | 277.3 | - |

- Where the main stream finished last in the base (c = 4 and c >= 32), the metadata now runs in the router stream's slack: the experts start 2.5-4.5 µs earlier.
- Where the router stream already finished last (c = 1-2) or the streams tied (c = 8-16), the metadata stays on the critical path behind the router, so the saving is the join-to-metadata gap and a faster metadata kernel on the router stream: 0.6-2.5 µs.
- With this PR the router stream finishes last at every concurrency where the split runs, so shortening the router GEMM is the next lever.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: perf | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

`RoutedMoeSplit` always runs FlashInfer's untuned default tile and config (`DABody(tactic=-1, ...)`). Autotune is on by default here: the Muse Spark hook picks `flashinfer_trtllm` on SM10x, and `EagerRunner` runs autotune before graph capture. Without this PR, the captured routed call uses the tuned `[tile_N, config]` from `AutoTuner.choose_one`. With this PR, captured graphs in the split range drop it.

**Why it matters**

The speed tables used autotune off on both sides, so they do not show that the gain holds in the default config.

**Fix**

Run the tuned tactic and build the metadata for its tile, or keep the split off when autotune is on. Otherwise, post before/after numbers with autotune on.

+"""FlashInfer's FP4 routed MoE split into routing metadata and the expert body.
+
+The routing metadata only needs the packed top-k ids, so it can be built on the router stream while the
+main stream quantizes activations; the main stream then launches the expert body alone. Output matches
+trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe(do_finalize=False) with the default (untuned) tile and config.
+
+Adapted from FlashInfer 0.7.2: the runner and arguments in ``RoutedMoeSplit.run_body`` from
+``trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe_op`` (flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py), and ``_default_tile`` from
+``selectDefaultTileN`` (csrc/trtllm_fused_moe_kernel_launcher.cu). flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8050 makes
+the body-only call public as ``trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe(..., routing_metadata=...)``; switch
+``run_body`` to it once SGLang requires a FlashInfer release that has it.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Optional
+
+import torch
+from flashinfer.fused_moe import core
+from flashinfer.fused_moe.core import (
+    MoeRunnerInputs,
+    populate_trtllm_moe_routing_metadata_,
+    trtllm_moe_allocate_routing_metadata_multi_tile,
+)
+from flashinfer.fused_moe.da_moe import DABody
+from flashinfer.tllm_enums import (
+    Fp8QuantizationType,
+    RoutingInputMode,
+    WeightLayout,
+    deduce_trtllm_gen_tensor_dtype,
+)
+
+# FlashInfer's NvFP4 x NvFP4 tile candidates; sync with selectDefaultTileN.
+_FP4_TILES = (8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 192, 256)
+# Measured range: decode up to c = 128 with 8 draft tokens. FlashInfer's own bound is
+# trtllm_moe_max_da_multi_tile_tokens(num_experts), 2048 at 256 experts.
+_MAX_SPLIT_TOKENS = 1024
+# FlashInfer 0.7.2 builds no tile-192 FP4 kernel for SM107, while _FP4_TILES (GB300's list) has one;
+# cap the split at tile 128 so it never asks for a tile the build lacks. FlashInfer main ships
+# SM107 tile 192 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8050 tests it); drop the cap with the switch to that API.
+_MAX_SPLIT_TILE = 128
+
+
+def _default_tile(*, num_tokens: int, top_k: int, num_local_experts: int) -> int:
+    """The tile FlashInfer picks without a tuned tactic: one below the tile covering tokens per expert."""
+    per_expert = num_tokens * top_k / num_local_experts
+    i = next(
+        (k for k, t in enumerate(_FP4_TILES) if t >= per_expert), len(_FP4_TILES) - 1
+    )
+    return _FP4_TILES[max(i - 1, 0)]
+
+
+# Smallest token count from which the split was measured to beat the fused routing, per
+# (compute capability, TP size); unlisted configurations keep the fused routing. SM107 gains at every
+# measured decode size (M = 8-1024, DFlash 8 tokens). GB300 (10, 3) is unlisted: with the cuBLAS router
+# GEMM its router stream gates the experts at nearly every token count, so the split only adds overhead.
+_SPLIT_MIN_TOKENS: dict[tuple[tuple[int, int], int], int] = {
+    ((10, 7), 4): 8,
+    ((10, 7), 8): 8,
+}
+
+
+def split_enabled(
+    *, num_tokens: int, tp_size: int, capability: tuple[int, int]
+) -> bool:
+    min_tokens = _SPLIT_MIN_TOKENS.get((tuple(capability), tp_size))
+    return min_tokens is not None and num_tokens >= min_tokens
+
+
+def split_supported(*, num_tokens: int, top_k: int, num_local_experts: int) -> bool:
+    return (
+        num_tokens <= _MAX_SPLIT_TOKENS
+        and _default_tile(
+            num_tokens=num_tokens, top_k=top_k, num_local_experts=num_local_experts
+        )
+        <= _MAX_SPLIT_TILE
+    )
+
+
+class RoutedMoeSplit:
+    """Graph-stable routing metadata for one token count, shared by all layers.
+
+    Layers run in order on both streams: the router stream forks from main after the previous
+    layer's body and its deferred finalize, so a populate never overwrites metadata still being read.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        packed_topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        num_experts: int,
+        local_expert_offset: int,
+        num_local_experts: int,
+    ):
+        num_tokens, top_k = packed_topk_ids.shape
+        self.tile_n = _default_tile(
+            num_tokens=num_tokens, top_k=top_k, num_local_experts=num_local_experts
+        )
+        self._metadata = trtllm_moe_allocate_routing_metadata_multi_tile(
+            packed_topk_ids,
+            num_experts=num_experts,
+            top_k=top_k,
+            local_expert_offset=local_expert_offset,
+            num_local_experts=num_local_experts,
+            tile_ns=(self.tile_n,),
+            routing_input_mode=RoutingInputMode.PackedPrecomputed,
+        )
+        self._slot = self._metadata.slots[0]
+        self._body = DABody(tactic=-1, tile_n=self.tile_n)

+"""Muse Spark routed MoE split: metadata + body must match the ordinary FlashInfer call bitwise."""

+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci

+    ).to(torch.int32)

+    return hs, sf, packed, scale

+        routing_bias=None,

+        gemm1_weights=view["gemm1_weights"],
+        gemm1_weights_scale=view["gemm1_weights_scale"],
+        gemm1_bias=None,
+        gemm1_alpha=view.get("gemm1_alpha"),
+        gemm1_beta=None,
+        gemm1_clamp_limit=None,
+        gemm2_weights=view["gemm2_weights"],
+        gemm2_weights_scale=view["gemm2_weights_scale"],
+        gemm2_bias=None,
+        output1_scale_scalar=view.get("output1_scale_scalar"),

+        per_token_scale=scale,

+        intermediate_size=I,

+        local_num_experts=local,
+        routed_scaling_factor=1.0,
+        routing_method_type=1,

+        main.wait_stream(side)

+        captured = run()
+    for seed in (m + 1, m + 2):
+        new_hs, new_sf, new_packed, new_scale = _inputs(quant, m, seed, per_token)
+        hs.copy_(new_hs)
+        sf.copy_(new_sf)
+        packed.copy_(new_packed)
+        if per_token:
+            scale.copy_(new_scale)
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(_finalize(m, *captured), _ordinary(kwargs, m)), (
+            f"replay seed={seed}"
+        )

+    assert not split_supported(num_tokens=960, top_k=TOP_K, num_local_experts=32)

<!-- PR title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] muse-spark: Build the routed-MoE routing metadata on the router stream -->

## Motivation

In a decode MoE layer two streams run after the attention boundary:

- main stream: the pre-expert projection (pooler), the all-gather, then the pre-expert RMSNorm + NVFP4 quant;
- router stream: the router GEMM and the top-8 routing.

After the two streams join, the main stream calls FlashInfer's `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`, which first builds the routing metadata and then runs the expert GEMMs. The metadata depends only on the top-8 ids, so it does not need to wait for the main stream.

This PR builds the routing metadata on the router stream right after the top-8, and the main stream runs only the expert GEMMs after the join.

**GB300 is not affected by this PR.**

## Modifications

- `routed_moe_split.py` (new): `RoutedMoeSplit` holds the routing metadata for one token count, shared by all layers; `populate()` builds it on the router stream and `run_body()` launches FlashInfer's expert body from it. It uses FlashInfer 0.7.2's prepared-routing objects (`DABodyRunner`), with the runner and arguments adapted from `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe_op`. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8050 makes this a public argument (`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe(..., routing_metadata=...)`); `run_body` switches to it once SGLang requires a FlashInfer release that has it.
- `routed_moe_split.py`: `split_enabled` gates the split by `_SPLIT_MIN_TOKENS[(capability, tp)]`, the measured smallest token count where it wins (SM107 TP4 / TP8: 8); unlisted (GPU, TP) pairs keep the fused routing.
- `muse_spark.py`: `MuseSpark1xMoE` builds the split on the router stream after the top-8 when it applies (NVFP4, not Marlin, decode CUDA graph capture, enabled for this GPU and TP, M <= 1024 and FlashInfer's default tile <= 128) and passes it to the experts. `routed_moe_split` (and the FlashInfer internals it uses) is imported only once the cheap checks pass, so importing the model does not import it.
- `muse_spark_fp4_moe.py`: the experts call `moe_split.run_body` instead of `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` when a split is given; the arguments and outputs are the same.

The expert body's buffers are allocated per call like the ordinary routed call, so under CUDA graph capture they come from the graph pool shared by every captured batch size; only the routing metadata (a few small buffers per token count) is kept.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

The expert outputs are bitwise those of the ordinary routed call, so model outputs do not change.

Muse Spark Open + this PR, DFlash (real acceptance), sgl-eval with T=1.0, top_p=1.0, top_k=64, xhigh reasoning; GSM8K max 65K tokens, AIME26 30 problems x 16 repeats, max 131K tokens.

| GPU | TP | GSM8K | AIME26 pass@1 | AIME26 pass@16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SM107 | 4 | 97.65% | 96.67% | 100% |

<details>
<summary>Kernel tests</summary>

`test_muse_spark_routed_moe_split.py` (registered on `4-gpu-b200`, one GPU), bitwise against `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe(do_finalize=False)` (per-token weighted sum of the expert outputs): 64 local experts of 256 at M in {1, 16, 128, 512, 1024} and 32 local experts at M in {1, 16, 128, 512, 768} (TP4 / TP8 with EP), each with static and per-token activation scales. As in serving, the metadata is populated on a side stream and the main stream waits on it before the body; a CUDA graph of that sequence is then replayed twice with new routing and new activations copied into its inputs, each replay checked against an ordinary call on the same inputs. Gate tests assert the listed cases are admitted, tile 192 / M > 1024 are not, and only the measured (GPU, TP) pairs enable the split.

- SM107: 22 / 22 passed.

This PR requires the pinned FlashInfer 0.7.2: on 0.7.0.post1 the prepared body at tile 128 (32 local experts, M = 768) writes NaN into valid FC2 rows, while on 0.7.2 it is bitwise equal to the ordinary call.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

**Setup.** Base = our Muse decode stack with #47517 (fused all-gather + norm + NVFP4 quant), this PR = the same stack + this PR; FlashInfer autotune off and per-token NVFP4 activation off on both sides.

+"""FlashInfer's FP4 routed MoE split into routing metadata and the expert body.

+The routing metadata only needs the packed top-k ids, so it can be built on the router stream while the
+main stream quantizes activations; the main stream then launches the expert body alone. Output matches
+trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe(do_finalize=False) with the default (untuned) tile and config.

+``trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe_op`` (flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py), and ``_default_tile`` from
+``selectDefaultTileN`` (csrc/trtllm_fused_moe_kernel_launcher.cu). flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8050 makes
+the body-only call public as ``trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe(..., routing_metadata=...)``; switch

+    RoutingInputMode,
+    WeightLayout,
+    deduce_trtllm_gen_tensor_dtype,
+)

+# cap the split at tile 128 so it never asks for a tile the build lacks. FlashInfer main ships
+# SM107 tile 192 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8050 tests it); drop the cap with the switch to that API.
+_MAX_SPLIT_TILE = 128
+
+
+def _default_tile(*, num_tokens: int, top_k: int, num_local_experts: int) -> int:
+    """The tile FlashInfer picks without a tuned tactic: one below the tile covering tokens per expert."""
+    per_expert = num_tokens * top_k / num_local_experts
+    i = next(
+        (k for k, t in enumerate(_FP4_TILES) if t >= per_expert), len(_FP4_TILES) - 1
+    )
+    return _FP4_TILES[max(i - 1, 0)]

+
+# Smallest token count from which the split was measured to beat the fused routing, per
+# (compute capability, TP size); unlisted configurations keep the fused routing. SM107 gains at every
+# measured decode size (M = 8-1024, DFlash 8 tokens). GB300 (10, 3) is unlisted: with the cuBLAS router

+_SPLIT_MIN_TOKENS: dict[tuple[tuple[int, int], int], int] = {
+    ((10, 7), 4): 8,
+    ((10, 7), 8): 8,
+}
+
+
+def split_enabled(
+    *, num_tokens: int, tp_size: int, capability: tuple[int, int]
+) -> bool:
+    min_tokens = _SPLIT_MIN_TOKENS.get((tuple(capability), tp_size))
+    return min_tokens is not None and num_tokens >= min_tokens
+
+
+def split_supported(*, num_tokens: int, top_k: int, num_local_experts: int) -> bool:
+    return (
+        num_tokens <= _MAX_SPLIT_TOKENS
+        and _default_tile(
+            num_tokens=num_tokens, top_k=top_k, num_local_experts=num_local_experts
+        )
+        <= _MAX_SPLIT_TILE
+    )
+
+
+class RoutedMoeSplit:
+    """Graph-stable routing metadata for one token count, shared by all layers.
+
+    Layers run in order on both streams: the router stream forks from main after the previous
+    layer's body and its deferred finalize, so a populate never overwrites metadata still being read.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        packed_topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        num_experts: int,
+        local_expert_offset: int,
+        num_local_experts: int,
+    ):

+            num_tokens=num_tokens, top_k=top_k, num_local_experts=num_local_experts

+        self._metadata = trtllm_moe_allocate_routing_metadata_multi_tile(
+            packed_topk_ids,

+            num_local_experts=num_local_experts,

+            routing_input_mode=RoutingInputMode.PackedPrecomputed,

+            gemm1_weights=gemm1_weights,

+            gemm1_bias=gemm1_bias,

+            gemm2_weights=gemm2_weights,
+            gemm2_weights_scale=gemm2_weights_scale,
+            gemm2_bias=gemm2_bias,
+            output1_scale_scalar=output1_scale_scalar,
+            output1_scale_gate_scalar=output1_scale_gate_scalar,
+            output2_scale_scalar=output2_scale_scalar,
+            n_group=n_group,
+            topk_group=topk_group,

+            local_expert_offset=local_expert_offset,
+            num_local_experts=num_local_experts,
+        )

Run the tuned tactic and build the metadata for its tile, or keep the split off when autotune is on. Otherwise, post before/after numbers with autotune on.

+# cap the split at tile 128 so it never asks for a tile the build lacks. FlashInfer main ships
+# SM107 tile 192 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8050 tests it); drop the cap with the switch to that API.
+_MAX_SPLIT_TILE = 128
+
+
+def _default_tile(*, num_tokens: int, top_k: int, num_local_experts: int) -> int:
+    """The tile FlashInfer picks without a tuned tactic: one below the tile covering tokens per expert."""
+    per_expert = num_tokens * top_k / num_local_experts
+    i = next(
+        (k for k, t in enumerate(_FP4_TILES) if t >= per_expert), len(_FP4_TILES) - 1
+    )
+    return _FP4_TILES[max(i - 1, 0)]

+    ((10, 7), 4): 8,
+    ((10, 7), 8): 8,

+

+def split_enabled(
+    *, num_tokens: int, tp_size: int, capability: tuple[int, int]
+) -> bool:
+    min_tokens = _SPLIT_MIN_TOKENS.get((tuple(capability), tp_size))
+    return min_tokens is not None and num_tokens >= min_tokens
+

+        packed_topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
